requiredFindings.title: Glob classification still consults repository evidence below pruned anchors
requiredFindings.problem: The literal-entry placement walk now stops at anchors, but the npm glob branch searches every directory in inp["fs"] and calls _markers on it without applying pruning or the observed boundary population. Consequently a positive VCS fact hidden below W/.opensip changes workspaceDeclarations even though that exact anchor must never be entered and its descendants are absent from discovery. The same behavior occurs below node_modules. This leaves the no-hidden-observation part of round 1 RF-1 incomplete through another entry path.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Classify glob crossings from the legally observable repository/boundary population, stopping at exact/pruned anchors before consulting descendants. Preserve crossings proved by a visible enclosing repository without opening its protected subtrees. Add paired fixtures differing only in a repository hidden below W/.opensip and a dependency anchor, plus metadata-observation spies; the hidden addition must not change the reader disposition or be consulted. Extend the controls beyond provider-content reads, and refresh the pinned checks and successor artifacts.
evidence: With W=/h/w, its ordinary project carrier, an empty W/.opensip directory and package.json workspaces=[".opensip/*"], discover returns ACCEPT with no unresolved npm entry.
Adding only W/.opensip/secret with vcs=True and its .git directory changes that result to workspace-glob-crosses-repository; nestedRepositories remains empty in both results.
The same paired change under node_modules changes the disposition of node_modules/* while leaving those paths pruned.
The comprehension at lines 474-476 reads the raw supplied map instead of the population used by _finish; the current content-read spies do not cover this metadata path.
